study type: Cross-sectional study (analysis of retrospective survey data)
cohort: The study included 2126 post-neonates born from mothers interviewed about births in the five years before the 2019 Ethiopia mini demographic and health survey.
finding: Several factors were significantly associated with post-neonatal death, including non-vaccination of infants, lack of maternal tetanus injection, young maternal age, residence in specific regions, higher birth order, lack of antenatal care, short birth intervals, and being a multiple birth, while exclusive breastfeeding, urban residence, fewer children, and male household head were associated with lower risk.
cross-section timing: Data gathered from March 21, 2019, to June 28, 2019
